question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Government by one person who holds absolute power.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Autocracy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Autocracy" means government by one person with absolute power, from the Greek “autos” (self) and “kratos” (power, rule). (एकतंत्र/निरंकुश शासन)
◦ Example: The king ruled the small nation as an autocracy, answering to no one.

 

• The suffix "-cracy" always denotes a system or form of government/rule, and the first part of the word tells us who or what holds the power.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Democracy (लोकतंत्र): Government by the people, exercised through elected representatives, from the Greek “demos” (people).

 

• Option 3: Aristocracy (अभिजात वर्ग का शासन): Government by a small privileged ruling class, from the Greek “aristos” (best).

 

• Option 4: Theocracy (धर्मतंत्र): Government by religious leaders claiming divine authority, from the Greek “theos” (god).

 

NOTE

 

• Other "-cracy/-crat" words frequently asked in SSC: Bureaucracy (officials/administrators), Plutocracy (the wealthy), Meritocracy (those of talent or merit), Mobocracy (the mob or crowd), Gerontocracy (the elderly), and Technocracy (technical experts).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Sybarite (भोग-विलासी): A person devoted to luxury and pleasure

2. Bibliophile (पुस्तक प्रेमी): A person who loves and collects books

3. Chauvinist (अंधराष्ट्रवादी): A person with excessive, blind loyalty to their own group

4. Dilettante (शौकिया कलाप्रेमी): A person with a superficial interest in an art

5. Epicure (स्वादिष्ट भोजन का शौकीन): A person with refined taste in food and drink

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who dislikes, distrusts, or is prejudiced against men.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Misandrist.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Misandrist" means a person who dislikes or is prejudiced against men, from the Greek “misein” (to hate) and “aner/andros” (man). (पुरुष द्वेषी)
◦ Example: As a committed misandrist, she refused to work under any male supervisor.

 

• The prefix "mis-" combined with a Greek root always denotes hatred or dislike of the thing named by that root, e.g. "-gyny" (women), "-andry" (men), and "-anthropy" (mankind).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Misogynist (स्त्री-द्वेषी): A person who dislikes, despises, or is prejudiced against women, from the Greek “misein” (to hate) and “gyne” (woman).

 

• Option 3: Philanderer (स्त्रीलंपट पुरुष): A man who engages in numerous casual love affairs with women.

 

• Option 4: Misanthrope (मानव-द्वेषी): A person who dislikes or distrusts humankind in general, from the Greek “misein” (to hate) and “anthropos” (human).

 

NOTE

 

• Other "mis-" words frequently asked in SSC: Misogamist (one who hates marriage), Misoneist (one who hates change or novelty), Misologist (one who distrusts reasoning or argument), and Misocapnist (one who hates tobacco smoke).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Fastidious (चूजी): Very attentive to detail and hard to please

2. Garrulous (बातूनी): Excessively talkative

3. Hedonist (सुखवादी): A person who believes pleasure is life's highest good

4. Iconoclast (परंपरा भंजक): A person who attacks cherished beliefs or traditions

5. Jingoist (युद्धोन्मादी राष्ट्रवादी): An extreme, aggressive nationalist

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Persons who live or occur during the same period of time as one another.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Contemporaries.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Contemporaries" means persons living or occurring at the same time as one another, from the Latin “con” (together) and “tempus” (time). (समकालीन)
◦ Example: Einstein and Bohr were contemporaries who often debated the nature of reality.

 

• The prefix "con-" (from Latin, meaning "together" or "with") appears in many words denoting joint action or shared state, such as "concurrent," "coexist," and "correspond."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Predecessors (पूर्ववर्ती): Persons who held a position or office before someone else, from the Latin “prae” (before) and “cedere” (to go).

 

• Option 2: Successors (उत्तराधिकारी): Persons who follow and take over the position of another.

 

• Option 4: Descendants (वंशज): Persons who are descended from a particular ancestor.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Contemporaries" frequently asked in SSC: Coevals (persons of the same age or era), Peers (persons of equal standing), Compeers (equals or associates), and Colleagues (people one works with).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Loquacious (वाचाल): Tending to talk a great deal

2. Megalomaniac (महत्वाकांक्षा उन्माद से ग्रस्त व्यक्ति): A person with an obsessive desire for power

3. Nomad (खानाबदोश): A person who moves from place to place with no fixed home

4. Omnivorous (सर्वभक्षी): Eating both plant and animal food

5. Philatelist (डाक टिकट संग्रहकर्ता): A person who collects postage stamps

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

One who promotes the welfare of others, especially by donating money to good causes.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Philanthropist.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Philanthropist" means a person who promotes the welfare of others, especially by donating money, from the Greek “philein” (to love) and “anthropos” (mankind). (परोपकारी)
◦ Example: The billionaire philanthropist donated most of his fortune to fight malaria.

 

• The prefix "phil-/philo-" always denotes a love or fondness for the thing named in the rest of the word, e.g. "-anthropy" (mankind), "-ately" (postage stamps), "-ology" (a field of study).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Philatelist (डाक टिकट संग्रहकर्ता): A person who collects and studies postage stamps, from the Greek “philos” (loving) and “ateleia” (exemption from further charge, referring to prepaid postage).

 

• Option 2: Philanderer (स्त्रीलंपट पुरुष): A man who engages in numerous casual love affairs with women.

 

• Option 3: Philologist (भाषाशास्त्री): A person who studies language and linguistics, especially historical and comparative linguistics.

 

NOTE

 

• Other "phil-" words frequently asked in SSC: Bibliophile (books), Anglophile (England/English things), Xenophile (foreigners), Audiophile (high-quality sound reproduction), and Technophile (technology).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Quack (नीम-हकीम): A person who dishonestly claims to have medical knowledge

2. Recluse (एकांतवासी): A person who lives in self-imposed isolation

3. Sycophant (चापलूस): A person who flatters others to gain personal advantage

4. Teetotaler (मद्यत्यागी): A person who never drinks alcohol

5. Vagabond (आवारा): A person who wanders from place to place with no home

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Property or an estate inherited from one's father or male ancestors.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Patrimony.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Patrimony" means property or an estate inherited from one's father or male ancestors, from the Latin “pater” (father). (पैतृक संपत्ति)
◦ Example: He sold off the family patrimony to settle his debts.

 

• The suffix "-mony" (from Latin “-monium”) denotes a state, condition, or result, as seen in "matrimony" (the state of marriage), "alimony," and "testimony."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Matrimony (विवाह): The state or ceremony of being married, from the Latin “mater” (mother) via “matrimonium.”

 

• Option 3: Alimony (गुजारा भत्ता): Money that a person is legally required to pay to their spouse after separation or divorce.

 

• Option 4: Testimony (गवाही): A formal written or spoken statement, especially one given in a court of law.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Patrimony" frequently asked in SSC: Heritage (inherited property or tradition), Legacy (money or property left in a will), Inheritance (assets passed to an heir), and Ancestral property (property passed down through generations).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Xenophobe (विदेशी-द्वेषी): A person who fears or hates foreigners

2. Zealot (कट्टर समर्थक): A person fanatically committed to a cause

3. Ascetic (तपस्वी): A person who practises strict self-denial for religious reasons

4. Cynic (निंदक): A person who believes people act only out of self-interest

5. Diplomat (राजनयिक): A person who conducts negotiations on behalf of a country

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A fictitious name adopted by an author to conceal their real identity.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Pseudonym.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Pseudonym" means a fictitious name adopted by an author to conceal their real identity, from the Greek “pseudes” (false) and “onyma” (name). (छद्म नाम/उपनाम)
◦ Example: Mark Twain was the pseudonym of the writer Samuel Clemens.

 

• The suffix "-onym" always denotes a name or word, and the first part of the word tells us what kind of name it is, e.g. "pseudo-" (false), "syn-" (same), "acro-" (topmost letters).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Synonym (पर्यायवाची): A word or phrase that has the same or nearly the same meaning as another, from the Greek “syn” (together/same) and “onyma” (name).

 

• Option 3: Eponym (अभिनाम): A person after whom a discovery, place, or era is named, from the Greek “epi” (upon) and “onyma” (name).

 

• Option 4: Acronym (संक्षिप्ताक्षर): A word formed from the initial letters of a phrase, from the Greek “akros” (topmost) and “onyma” (name).

 

NOTE

 

• Other "-onym" words frequently asked in SSC: Antonym (a word of opposite meaning), Homonym (a word with the same spelling or sound but a different meaning), Anonym (a name that is not made known), Toponym (a name derived from a place), and Cryptonym (a code name).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Egoist (अहंवादी): A person who is excessively self-centered

2. Fanatic (कट्टरपंथी): A person filled with excessive, uncritical enthusiasm for a cause

3. Glutton (पेटू): A person who eats and drinks excessively

4. Herbivore (शाकाहारी प्राणी): An animal that feeds only on plants

5. Introvert (अंतर्मुखी व्यक्ति): A shy, reticent person absorbed in their own thoughts

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person with a recurrent, uncontrollable urge to steal, not out of economic need.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Kleptomaniac.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Kleptomaniac" means a person with a recurrent, uncontrollable urge to steal, from the Greek “kleptein” (to steal) and “mania” (madness, obsession). (चोरी करने की बीमारी वाला)
◦ Example: Store security kept a close eye on the known kleptomaniac.

 

• The suffix "-maniac" always denotes a person with an obsessive or uncontrollable urge, and the first part of the word tells us what that urge is directed toward.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Pyromaniac (अग्नि-उन्माद से ग्रस्त व्यक्ति): A person with an obsessive urge to start fires, from the Greek “pyr” (fire).

 

• Option 2: Egomaniac (अहं-उन्माद से ग्रस्त व्यक्ति): A person who is obsessively self-centered or preoccupied with their own importance.

 

• Option 4: Monomaniac (एकल-विचार उन्माद से ग्रस्त व्यक्ति): A person obsessed with a single idea or subject.

 

NOTE

 

• Other "-maniac" words frequently asked in SSC: Nymphomaniac (excessive sexual desire), Dipsomaniac (an uncontrollable craving for alcohol), Bibliomaniac (an excessive love of collecting books), Megalomaniac (an obsessive desire for power), and Monomaniac (an obsession with a single idea).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Juggernaut (विशाल अजेय शक्ति): A huge, overwhelming, unstoppable force or institution

2. Linguist (भाषाविद्): A person skilled in foreign languages or the study of language

3. Maverick (स्वतंत्र विचारक): An unorthodox, independent-minded person

4. Optimist (आशावादी): A person who tends to expect the best outcome

5. Pessimist (निराशावादी): A person who expects the worst outcome

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who has, or professes to have, a special appreciation of art and beauty.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Aesthete.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Aesthete" means a person with a special appreciation of art and beauty, from the Greek “aisthetikos” (perceptive, sensitive to beauty). (कला प्रेमी/सौंदर्यप्रेमी)
◦ Example: As a true aesthete, she filled her home with fine paintings and sculpture.

 

• "Aesthete" is frequently confused with the similarly spelled "Ascetic" (a person who practises strict self-denial), so SSC papers often set the two as trap options.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Ascetic (तपस्वी): A person who practises severe self-discipline and abstains from worldly pleasures, often for religious reasons.

 

• Option 2: Anesthetist (निश्चेतक चिकित्सक): A medical professional who administers anesthesia to patients before surgery.

 

• Option 3: Athlete (खिलाड़ी): A person who competes in one or more sports involving physical strength, speed, or endurance.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Aesthete" frequently asked in SSC: Connoisseur (an expert judge in matters of art or taste), Dilettante (a person with a superficial interest in an art), Epicure (a person with refined taste in food and wine), and Virtuoso (a person highly skilled in an art, especially music).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Recidivist (बार-बार अपराध करने वाला): A convicted criminal who reoffends repeatedly

2. Stoic (अविचल व्यक्ति): A person who endures hardship without complaint

3. Tyro (नौसिखिया): A beginner or novice in a field

4. Yokel (देहाती व्यक्ति): An unsophisticated person from a rural area

5. Workaholic (काम में डूबा व्यक्ति): A person addicted to working

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A state of temporary disuse or suspension.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Abeyance.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Abeyance" means a state of temporary disuse, suspension, or inactivity, from the Old French “abeance,” a legal term for a state of expectancy. (ठहराव/निलंबन)
◦ Example: The project was held in abeyance until fresh funding arrived.

 

• The phrase "held in abeyance" is a common legal/administrative collocation meaning temporarily set aside or suspended, often used regarding decisions, laws, or claims awaiting further action.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Ambience (वातावरण): The character and atmosphere of a particular place.

 

• Option 3: Allegiance (निष्ठा): Loyalty or commitment to a superior, group, or cause.

 

• Option 4: Abstinence (संयम/परहेज़): The practice of restraining oneself from indulging in something, such as food, alcohol, or pleasure.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Abeyance" frequently asked in SSC: Dormancy (a state of inactivity), Suspension (a temporary halting of an activity), Moratorium (a temporary prohibition or delay), and Hiatus (a pause or gap in continuity).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Zoophobe (पशु-भीति से ग्रस्त व्यक्ति): A person who has an abnormal fear of animals

2. Bibliophobe (पुस्तक-भीति से ग्रस्त व्यक्ति): A person who fears or hates books

3. Nostalgia (अतीत की याद): A sentimental longing for a past time or place

4. Utopia (काल्पनिक आदर्श समाज): An imagined place or state in which everything is perfect

5. Vegetarian (शाकाहारी व्यक्ति): A person who does not eat meat or fish

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Fond of the company of others; sociable.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Gregarious.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Gregarious" means fond of the company of others; sociable, from the Latin “grex/gregis” (a flock or herd). (मिलनसार)
◦ Example: He was a gregarious host who loved throwing large parties.

 

• The Latin root "greg" (meaning a flock or group) also appears in "congregate" (to gather in a crowd), "segregate" (to set apart from a group), and "aggregate" (to combine into a total).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Reticent (मितभाषी/संकोची): Reluctant to speak freely or reveal one's thoughts and feelings.

 

• Option 3: Reclusive (एकांतप्रिय): Avoiding the company of others; preferring to live in solitude.

 

• Option 4: Taciturn (मौन/कम बोलने वाला): Reserved and saying very little; habitually uncommunicative.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Gregarious" frequently asked in SSC: Sociable (fond of the company of others), Convivial (friendly, lively, and enjoying company), Amicable (friendly and good-natured), and Genial (warm and friendly in disposition).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Antagonist (विरोधी/प्रतिद्वंद्वी): A person who actively opposes or is hostile to another

2. Protagonist (नायक/प्रमुख पात्र): The leading character in a drama or story

3. Connoisseur (पारखी): An expert judge in matters of art or taste

4. Virtuoso (निपुण कलाकार): A person highly skilled in an art, especially music

5. Skeptic (संशयवादी): A person inclined to question or doubt accepted beliefs

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Unable to read or write.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Illiterate.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Illiterate" means unable to read or write, from the Latin “in-” (not) and “litteratus” (lettered, learned). (अनपढ़/निरक्षर)
◦ Example: Nearly a third of the village's elderly population is still illiterate.

 

• The prefix "il-" is a variant of the negative prefix "in-" used before words beginning with "l" (e.g., illegal, illegible, illiterate) and always denotes "not."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Literate (साक्षर): Able to read and write.

 

• Option 2: Numerate (अंकज्ञ): Having a good basic understanding of arithmetic and mathematical concepts.

 

• Option 4: Erudite (विद्वान): Having or showing great knowledge gained from reading and study.

 

NOTE

 

• Other "il-/in-" negative-prefix words frequently asked in SSC: Illegible (not able to be read, of handwriting), Illegal (not lawful), Inarticulate (unable to express oneself clearly), Innumerable (too many to count), and Illegitimate (not authorized by law).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Sanguine (आशावादी/जोशीला): Optimistic and cheerful, even in a difficult situation

2. Melancholic (उदास/विषादग्रस्त): Having a feeling of thoughtful, deep sadness

3. Phlegmatic (शांत स्वभाव का): Having an unemotional, calm temperament

4. Choleric (क्रोधी स्वभाव का): Easily angered; bad-tempered

5. Apathetic (उदासीन): Showing little or no interest or concern

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person with an excessive interest in or admiration of their own self or appearance, marked by vanity and self-love.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Narcissist.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Narcissist" means a person with an excessive interest in or admiration of themselves, from the Greek myth of Narcissus, a youth who fell in love with his own reflection. (आत्ममुग्ध)
◦ Example: The narcissist spent hours each day admiring himself in the mirror.

 

• The suffix "-ist" generally denotes a person characterized by a particular belief, practice, or trait, though "Narcissist" is unusual in deriving from a proper name, an eponym, rather than a common Greek or Latin root.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Sycophant (चापलूस): A person who flatters others, especially those in power, to gain personal advantage.

 

• Option 2: Hypocrite (पाखंडी): A person who claims to have moral standards or beliefs that their behavior does not match.

 

• Option 3: Sadist (क्रूरतावादी/परपीड़क): A person who derives pleasure, especially sexual gratification, from inflicting pain or humiliation on others.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Narcissist" frequently asked in SSC: Egotist (a person excessively concerned with themselves), Vain (a person having excessive pride in their own appearance), Self-absorbed (preoccupied with oneself), and Conceited (excessively proud of oneself).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Nepotist (भाई-भतीजावाद करने वाला): A person who shows favoritism to relatives, especially in giving jobs

2. Plagiarist (साहित्यिक चोरी करने वाला): A person who copies another's work and passes it off as their own

3. Vandal (विध्वंसक): A person who deliberately destroys or damages property

4. Puritan (अतिशुद्धतावादी): A person with strict moral or religious views

5. Martinet (अनुशासनप्रिय कठोर व्यक्ति): A strict disciplinarian, especially in military matters

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

The art of producing decorative, beautiful handwriting.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Calligraphy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Calligraphy" means the art of producing decorative, beautiful handwriting, from the Greek “kallos” (beauty) and “graphein” (to write). (सुलेखन)
◦ Example: The ancient manuscript was admired for its exquisite calligraphy.

 

• The suffix "-graphy" always denotes a field of writing, recording, or representation, and the first part of the word tells us what is being written or recorded.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Cartography (मानचित्रकला): The science or practice of drawing maps, from the Greek “khartes” (map) and “graphein” (to write).

 

• Option 3: Choreography (नृत्य-रचना): The art of designing sequences of steps and movements for dance, from the Greek “khoreia” (dance) and “graphein” (to write).

 

• Option 4: Typography (मुद्रण-कला): The art or process of arranging type for printing, from the Greek “typos” (impression) and “graphein” (to write).

 

NOTE

 

• Other "-graphy" words frequently asked in SSC: Biography (a person's life story written by another), Autobiography (one's own life story written by oneself), Photography (the art of taking pictures using light), Stenography (the art of writing in shorthand), Geography (the study of the earth's physical features), Bibliography (a list of books or references used) and Lexicography (the compiling of dictionaries).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Sybarite (भोग-विलासी): A person excessively fond of luxury and pleasure

2. Misanthrope (मानव-द्वेषी): A person who dislikes or distrusts humankind

3. Bibliophile (पुस्तक-प्रेमी): A person who loves or collects books

4. Nomad (खानाबदोश): A person with no fixed home who moves from place to place

5. Ambidextrous (उभयहस्त): Able to use both hands equally well

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

The act of delaying or postponing tasks that should be done.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Procrastination.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Procrastination" means the habit of delaying or postponing tasks that should be done, from the Latin “pro” (forward) and “crastinus” (of tomorrow). (टालमटोल)
◦ Example: His procrastination meant the report was submitted a week late.

 

• Words built on the Latin root "cras" (tomorrow), like procrastination, relate to putting things off; note also how many abstract nouns of habit or process, such as this one, end in "-ation".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Vacillation (हिचकिचाहट): Repeated indecision or wavering between different opinions or courses of action.

 

• Option 3: Prevarication (बहानेबाजी): Speaking or acting evasively so as to avoid stating the truth directly.

 

• Option 4: Dereliction (कर्तव्य की उपेक्षा): The shameful neglect or abandonment of a duty or responsibility.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Procrastination" frequently asked in SSC: Dilatoriness (habitual slowness in acting or deciding), Tardiness (delay or lateness), Lethargy (a lack of energy or enthusiasm), Indolence (habitual laziness), Sloth (habitual disinclination to exertion) and Dawdling (wasting time by moving slowly).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Philatelist (डाक-टिकट संग्रहकर्ता): A person who collects postage stamps

2. Nostalgia (अतीत की याद): A sentimental longing for the past

3. Iconoclast (परंपरा-भंजक): A person who attacks cherished beliefs or institutions

4. Taciturn (मितभाषी): Reserved or uncommunicative in speech

5. Aficionado (शौकीन): A person who is very knowledgeable about an activity

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Characterized by the excessive use of long words.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Sesquipedalian.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Sesquipedalian" means characterized by the use of long words, from the Latin “sesqui” (one and a half) and “pes/pedis” (foot) — literally, a word a foot and a half long. (लंबे शब्दों का प्रयोग करने वाला)
◦ Example: The professor's sesquipedalian lecture left most students reaching for a dictionary.

 

• The Latin root "pes/pedis" (foot) also appears in words like "pedestrian" and "impediment"; here it combines with "sesqui" (one and a half) to humorously describe words long enough to be measured in feet.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Loquacious (बातूनी): Tending to talk a great deal; excessively talkative.

 

• Option 2: Laconic (अल्पभाषी): Using very few words; concise to the point of terseness.

 

• Option 4: Pedantic (पंडिताऊ): Excessively concerned with minor details, rules, or formal correctness, especially in a way that shows off learning.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Sesquipedalian" frequently asked in SSC: Verbose (using more words than needed), Bombastic (high-sounding language with little real meaning), Grandiloquent (pompous or inflated in language), Magniloquent (using lofty, extravagant language) and Periphrastic (using roundabout, indirect expression).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Panacea (रामबाण): A remedy for all ills or difficulties

2. Xenophobia (विदेशियों से भय/घृणा): An intense dislike or fear of foreigners

3. Connoisseur (पारखी): An expert judge in matters of art or taste

4. Nepotism (भाई-भतीजावाद): Favouritism shown to relatives in appointments

5. Somnambulist (नींद में चलने वाला): A person who walks about while asleep

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

One who uses astrology to predict the future by studying the positions of stars and planets.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Astrologer.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Astrologer" means a person who studies the positions of stars and planets in the belief that they influence human affairs, and uses this to predict the future, from the Greek “astron” (star) and “logos” (study). (ज्योतिषी)
◦ Example: The astrologer predicted a favourable year ahead based on the alignment of the planets.

 

• The suffix "-logist" (from the Greek “logos”) always denotes a person who studies or specialises in a subject; note the important contrast between astrology (celestial influence on human affairs) and astronomy (the scientific study of celestial objects).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Astronomer (खगोलशास्त्री): A scientist who studies celestial objects, space, and the physical universe, from the Greek “astron” (star) and “nomos” (law).

 

• Option 2: Numerologist (अंकशास्त्री): A person who studies the supposed mystical relationship between numbers and events.

 

• Option 3: Palmist (हस्तरेखा विशेषज्ञ): A person who reads the lines on a person's palm to foretell their future.

 

NOTE

 

• Other "-logist" words frequently asked in SSC: Geologist (rocks and the earth's structure), Archaeologist (ancient human history through excavation), Ornithologist (birds), Entomologist (insects), Numismatist (coins and currency) and Etymologist (the origin of words).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Utopia (काल्पनिक आदर्श समाज): An imagined perfect place or society

2. Vagabond (आवारा): A person who wanders about with no fixed home

3. Chauvinist (अंधराष्ट्रवादी): A person with excessive, biased devotion to their own group

4. Aristocracy (कुलीनतंत्र): Government or rule by a privileged upper class

5. Recluse (एकांतवासी): A person who lives in self-imposed isolation

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

An expression of sympathy offered to someone experiencing grief, sorrow, or misfortune.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Condolence.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Condolence" means an expression of sympathy offered to someone experiencing grief, sorrow, or misfortune, from the Latin “con” (together) and “dolere” (to grieve). (शोक संदेश)
◦ Example: Friends and relatives sent their condolences to the bereaved family.

 

• Other words built on the Latin root "dolere" (to suffer or grieve) include "doleful" (sad, mournful) and "indolent" (literally "without pain", i.e. avoiding effort); watch for this family in SSC vocabulary sets.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Eulogy (प्रशंसा भाषण): A speech or piece of writing that praises someone highly, typically a person who has recently died.

 

• Option 3: Elegy (शोकगीत): A mournful poem or song, typically composed as a lament for the dead.

 

• Option 4: Obituary (मृत्युलेख): A published notice of a person's death, usually with a short account of their life.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Condolence" frequently asked in SSC: Commiseration (an expression of sympathy or pity), Solace (comfort in a time of distress), Requiem (a mass or song for the repose of the dead), Eulogy (a speech praising the deceased) and Elegy (a mournful poem lamenting the dead).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Plagiarist (साहित्यिक चोर): A person who copies another's work and passes it off as their own

2. Homicide (मानव हत्या): The killing of one human being by another

3. Epicure (खाने-पीने का शौकीन): A person devoted to refined enjoyment of food and drink

4. Nocturnal (रात्रिचर): Active mainly during the night

5. Anachronism (कालविपर्यय): Something placed in the wrong historical time period

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

The practice of helping the poor and needy, typically through donations of money.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Philanthropy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Philanthropy" means the practice of helping the poor and needy, typically through the donation of money, from the Greek “philos” (loving) and “anthropos” (mankind). (परोपकार)
◦ Example: The billionaire's philanthropy funded schools and hospitals across the region.

 

• The prefix "phil-" always denotes love or fondness for something, while the suffix "-anthropy" relates to humankind; contrast this with "misanthropy", where the prefix "mis-" denotes hatred instead.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Misanthropy (मनुष्य जाति से घृणा): A general hatred, dislike, or distrust of humankind, from the Greek “misos” (hatred) and “anthropos” (mankind).

 

• Option 3: Patronage (संरक्षण): Support, encouragement, or financial backing given by a patron, not necessarily to the poor.

 

• Option 4: Philately (डाक टिकट संग्रह): The collection and study of postage stamps, from the Greek “philos” (loving) and “ateleia” (exemption from tax).

 

NOTE

 

• Other "phil-" words frequently asked in SSC: Bibliophile (one who loves books), Philatelist (one who collects stamps), Anglophile (one who admires England/English culture), Francophile (one who admires France), Xenophile (one attracted to foreign peoples/cultures) and Cynophile (one who loves dogs).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Hermit (सन्यासी): A person living in solitude, especially for religious reasons

2. Puritan (कठोर नैतिकतावादी): A person with strict moral or religious views

3. Deicide (ईश्वर-हत्या): The killing of a god

4. Agnostic (अज्ञेयवादी): A person who believes nothing can be known of God's existence

5. Maverick (स्वतंत्र विचारक): An unorthodox or independent-minded person

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A short, amusing or interesting story about a real incident or person.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Anecdote.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Anecdote" means a short, amusing or interesting story about a real incident or person, from the Greek “an-” (not) and “ekdotos” (published) — originally meaning unpublished, secret accounts. (किस्सा/लघुकथा)
◦ Example: She began her speech with a funny anecdote from her college days.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Allegory (रूपक): A story, poem, or picture that can be interpreted to reveal a hidden symbolic or moral meaning.

 

• Option 2: Parable (दृष्टांत कथा): A short, simple story used to illustrate a moral or spiritual lesson, typically religious.

 

• Option 4: Fable (नीतिकथा): A short story, typically featuring animals as characters, that conveys a moral lesson.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Anecdote" frequently asked in SSC: Parable (a short story conveying a moral or religious lesson), Fable (a short tale, often with animals, teaching a moral), Allegory (a story with a hidden symbolic meaning), Anthology (a collection of literary works) and Chronicle (a factual, chronological record of events).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Bigamist (द्विविवाही): A person who marries someone while still legally married to another

2. Zealot (कट्टर समर्थक): A person who is fanatically committed to a cause

3. Insomniac (अनिद्रा रोगी): A person who habitually finds it difficult to sleep

4. Cosmopolitan (विश्वबंधु): Familiar with and at ease in many different countries and cultures

5. Prodigy (अलौकिक प्रतिभा वाला व्यक्ति): A young person with exceptional talent or ability

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A disease prevalent throughout an entire country or the whole world.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Pandemic.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Pandemic" means a disease prevalent throughout an entire country or the whole world, from the Greek “pan” (all) and “demos” (people). (वैश्विक महामारी)
◦ Example: COVID-19 was declared a pandemic by the WHO in March 2020.

 

• The prefix "pan-" always denotes all or every; note the scale distinction between endemic (confined to one local population), epidemic (spreading widely within a region), and pandemic (spanning countries or the entire globe).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Epidemic (महामारी): A disease that spreads rapidly among many people in a community or region at a particular time, from the Greek “epi” (upon) and “demos” (people).

 

• Option 2: Endemic (स्थानिक रोग): A disease regularly found among a particular people or in a particular area, from the Greek “en” (in) and “demos” (people).

 

• Option 3: Outbreak (प्रकोप): A sudden rise in the occurrence of a disease, not necessarily widespread.

 

NOTE

 

• Other "pan-" words frequently asked in SSC: Panorama (a wide, unobstructed view), Panacea (a remedy for all ills), Pandemonium (wild uproar and chaos), Panoply (a complete or impressive array) and Panegyric (a formal speech of praise).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Ascetic (तपस्वी): A person who practices strict self-denial for spiritual reasons

2. Kleptomaniac (चोरी की उन्मत्त प्रवृत्ति वाला व्यक्ति): A person with an irresistible urge to steal

3. Dilettante (शौकिया): A person who dabbles in a subject without serious commitment

4. Genocide (नरसंहार): The deliberate killing of a large group of a particular nation or ethnicity

5. Altruist (परार्थवादी): A person unselfishly concerned for the welfare of others

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A government or state ruled or controlled by the wealthy.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Plutocracy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Plutocracy" means a government or state that is ruled or controlled by the wealthy, from the Greek “ploutos” (wealth) and “kratos” (power, rule). (धनिकतंत्र)
◦ Example: Critics argued that unchecked corporate influence was turning the democracy into a plutocracy.

 

• The suffix "-cracy" always denotes rule or government by a particular group, and the first part of the word tells us who holds the power; the related suffix "-crat" names a member of such a system, e.g. "aristocrat", "bureaucrat".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Aristocracy (कुलीनतंत्र): Government by a small privileged class, typically nobility, from the Greek “aristos” (best).

 

• Option 3: Bureaucracy (नौकरशाही): A system of government administered by officials following fixed rules and procedures.

 

• Option 4: Theocracy (धर्मतंत्र): Government by religious leaders or authority, exercised in the name of God or a deity.

 

NOTE

 

• Other "-cracy" words frequently asked in SSC: Democracy (rule by the people), Autocracy (rule by one person with absolute power), Meritocracy (rule by those with the greatest ability), Gerontocracy (rule by the elderly), Mobocracy (rule by the mob) and Technocracy (rule by technical experts).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Novice (नौसिखिया): A beginner in a particular skill or activity

2. Herbivorous (शाकाहारी): Feeding only on plants

3. Sadist (परपीड़क): A person who derives pleasure from inflicting pain on others

4. Widow (विधवा): A woman whose husband has died

5. Apostate (धर्मत्यागी): A person who abandons their religious faith

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

The practice of claiming to have moral standards or beliefs to which one's own behaviour does not conform.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Hypocrisy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Hypocrisy" means the practice of claiming to have moral standards or beliefs to which one's own behaviour does not conform, from the Greek “hypokrisis” (acting a part on stage, pretence). (पाखंड/ढोंग)
◦ Example: His public praise of honesty was pure hypocrisy given his own record of lying.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Sycophancy (चापलूसी): Excessive flattery or obsequious behaviour intended to gain advantage.

 

• Option 3: Bigotry (कट्टरता): Intolerance toward those holding different opinions, especially on religion, race, or politics.

 

• Option 4: Chicanery (छल-कपट): The use of trickery or deception, especially to achieve political, financial, or legal ends.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Hypocrisy" frequently asked in SSC: Duplicity (deliberate deceptiveness in behaviour), Sycophancy (excessive flattery to gain favour), Chicanery (use of trickery to achieve one's purpose), Cant (insincere talk about moral or religious matters) and Sanctimony (a hypocritical show of righteousness).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Carnivorous (मांसाहारी): Feeding on the flesh of other animals

2. Polyglot (बहुभाषाविद्): A person who knows and can use several languages

3. Martyr (शहीद): A person who suffers or dies for a cause or belief

4. Amnesty (सामान्य क्षमा): A general pardon, especially for political offences

5. Ostracize (बहिष्कृत करना): To exclude someone from a society or group

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

The attribution of human characteristics, emotions, or intentions to non-human beings, objects, or phenomena.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Anthropomorphism.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Anthropomorphism" means the attribution of human characteristics, emotions, or intentions to non-human beings, objects, or phenomena, from the Greek “anthropos” (human) and “morphe” (form). (मानवरूपण)
◦ Example: Cartoon animals that talk and wear clothes are common examples of anthropomorphism.

 

• The suffix "-morphism" (from the Greek “morphe”, form) always denotes taking on a particular shape or form; contrast anthropomorphism (human traits given to non-humans) with zoomorphism (animal traits given to humans or gods).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Anthropology (मानवशास्त्र): The scientific study of human beings, their societies, and cultures, past and present.

 

• Option 2: Personification (मानवीकरण): A literary device in which an abstract idea or inanimate object is given human qualities.

 

• Option 4: Zoomorphism (पशुरूपण): The attribution of animal characteristics or form to humans, gods, or objects.

 

NOTE

 

• Other "anthropo-" words frequently asked in SSC: Anthropology (the study of humankind), Anthropocentric (regarding humans as the central fact of the universe), Misanthrope (a hater of humankind), Philanthropy (love of humankind expressed through giving) and Lycanthropy (the mythical transformation of a human into a wolf).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Euphony (मधुर ध्वनि): A pleasant, harmonious sound, especially in speech

2. Spinster (अविवाहित स्त्री): An unmarried woman, typically an older one

3. Pyromaniac (अग्नि लगाने की असामान्य प्रवृत्ति वाला व्यक्ति): A person with an obsessive desire to start fires

4. Bibliomaniac (पुस्तकों के प्रति उन्मत्त प्रेम रखने वाला): A person with an extreme, obsessive passion for books

5. Truant (स्कूल से भागने वाला): A student who stays away from school without permission
